Why is it called a wake?

In the old days, there would be a vigil when a person died - mourners would watch over them from dusk till dawn, or until they were buried. So at least one person would be awake and sitting in a room with them all night, sometimes more than one. This was to double check they were really dead (and didn't 'wake), and possibly to some extent to prevent body snatching (I'm mostly kidding, but body snatching was a big thing during the early days of medicine).

Wakes are a time for the living to remember the dead, and while we now observe this in a shorter way, with a post-funeral gathering, the idea is that it is for the living rather than for the dead (aside for the 'checking they're dead' bit). I guess the fact that we can now definitely tell someone is dead, and body snatching has become much rarer, and funerals can now be a week or two later, we have stopped the practice of sitting up until the funeral, and have transferred it to after the funeral.
